chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar from Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Abdullah ibn Ayyub al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Amr al-Awza'i from Amr ibn Shimr from Salama ibn Kuhayl from Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) preached to the people in Medina.

He said: All praise is due to Allah, besides Whom there is no god. He was Alive without a 'how', and there was no 'being' for Him, nor was there a 'how' for His 'being', nor was there a 'where' for Him, nor was He in anything, nor upon anything, nor did He create a place for His 'being', nor did He become strong after creating something, nor was He weak before creating something, nor was He lonely before He began something, nor does He resemble anything, nor was He without dominion before He created it, nor will He be without it after it passes. He was a Living God without a lifespan, and a Master before He created anything, and a Master after He created the universe.

And for Allah there is no 'how' nor 'where', nor a limit to be recognized, nor anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to the duration of His remaining, nor does He weaken due to solitude, nor does He fear as His creatures fear something. But He is All-Hearing without hearing, All-Seeing without sight, and Almighty without strength from His creation. The pupils of the lookers cannot perceive Him, and the hearing of the listeners cannot encompass His hearing.

When He intends something, it is without consultation, or assistance, or informing, and He does not ask anyone about anything from His creation that He intended. The visions cannot perceive Him, but He perceives the visions. And He is the Subtle, the Aware. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, without a partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike it. So he conveyed the message and paved the way for guidance (peace be upon him and his family).

O community that was deceived and fell for the deception, and recognized the deception of the one who deceived it, but persisted upon what it recognized, and followed its desires, and wandered in the darkness of its misguidance. And the truth had become clear to it, so it turned away from it, and the path was clear, so it deviated from it.

By the One who split the grain and created the soul, had you drawn knowledge from its mine, and drunk water with its sweetness, and stored good from its place, and taken the path from its clarity, and followed the way of the truth, the paths would have been made clear for you, and the signs would have appeared to you, and Islam would have illuminated for you. So you would have eaten abundantly, and no poor person would have struggled among you, nor would any Muslim or ally have been wronged.

But you walked the path of darkness, so your world became dark for you by its vastness. And the doors of knowledge were closed to you, so you spoke according to your desires, and differed in your religion, so you issued verdicts in the religion of Allah without knowledge.

And you followed the misguided, so they misguided you, and you abandoned the Imams, so they abandoned you. So you became ruling by your desires. When a matter was mentioned, you asked the People of Remembrance, and when they issued a verdict to you, you said, 'This is the knowledge itself.' So how is it, when you have abandoned him, cast him aside, and opposed him? Slowly, after a little while, you will harvest all that you have sown, and find the evil of what you have committed and acquired.

By the One who split the grain and created the soul, you certainly know that I am your master and the one by whom you were commanded, and I am your knower and the one by whose knowledge is your salvation, and the successor of your Prophet, and the choice of your Lord, and the tongue of your light, and the knower of what rectifies you.

So after a little while, what has been promised to you and what descended upon the nations before you will descend upon you. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will question you about your Imams, with whom you will be gathered, and to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, you will return tomorrow.

By Allah, if I had the number of the companions of Talut, or the number of the people of Badr, and they were your enemies, I would have struck you with the sword until you returned to the truth and repented to the truth. So it would have been more suitable for the rift and more gentle. O Allah, judge between us with the truth, and You are the best of judges.

He said: Then he went out from the mosque and passed by a herd containing about thirty sheep. He said: By Allah, if I had men who would be sincere to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to His Messenger, in the number of these sheep, I would have removed the son of the eater of unclean things from his dominion.

He said: When it was evening, three hundred and sixty men had pledged allegiance to him for death. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Come with us to the Stones of Oil, shaved.' And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) shaved. None of the people remained loyal, shaved, except Abu Dharr, Al-Miqdad, Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, and Ammar ibn Yassir. And Salman came at the end of the people.

So he raised his hand to the sky and said: 'O Allah, the people have weakened me, just as the Children of Israel weakened Harun. O Allah, You know what we hide and what we proclaim, and nothing is hidden from You in the earth or in the sky. Make me die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.'

By the House, and the path leading to the House [and in one copy, Al-Muzdalifa], and the walking to the throwing of pebbles, had it not been for the oath that the Unlettered Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) made with me, I would have sent the opponents to the gulf of death, and I would have sent upon them the grey thunderbolts of death. And after a little while, they will know.

key_terms.أَحْجَارُ الزَّيْتِ: Stones of Oil (a place in Medina)
key_terms.ابْنُ آكِلَةِ الذِّبَّانِ: Son of the eater of unclean things (referring to Umayyads)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the attributes of Allah and the failure of the community in his sermon at Medina?
ai.summary: Known as the Sermon of Al-Ta'alutiyya, this address highlights the theological concept of 'Taqsim al-Akhbar' (dividing the news), where Ali (AS) withholds the immediate execution of justice to preserve the unity of Islam, citing the Prophet's oath. The sermon contrasts the community's deviation with the divine attributes of Allah, emphasizing that their failure to follow the Imams has led to spiritual and political decline, a theme central to Shia historiography regarding the transition from the Prophet's era to the Caliphate.

en.hubeali: H 14453 – Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ma’mar, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Ayyub Al-Ash’ary, from Amro Al-Awza’iy, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Salma Biin Kuheyl, from Abu Al-Haysam Bin Al-Tayhaan who has narrated: Amir-ul-Momineenasws gave a sermon to the people at Al-Medina.
